authorship.baseline: Individually authored concrete rule, code, or boundary scenarios. A488–833: offline_architecture; A834–1064: learning_design.
authorship.transfer: Individually authored per-point transfer scenarios B488–1064: offline_architecture.
authorship.explanations: Deterministic cleaned excerpts from the matching original knowledge point; this is source evidence, not independent expert validation.

verification: Complete two-item coverage for every integer point ID488–1064, unique question IDs and valid answer schemas.
A and B prompts differ and no item depends on a previous shuffled question.
Finite-width bit examples, recursive numeric examples, file-count examples and macro expansions checked against independent small mathematical models.
Input synonyms and alternative hexadecimal case are explicitly accepted where authored. Quoted two-option tasks become touch-friendly choice items without changing their meaning.

Final review clarified lower-bound indexing, positive odd-sum inputs, realloc size, binary-stream positions, character classification and implementation assumptions. Selected tasks use interactive code ordering.
limitations: These assessments consolidate the supplied C23 notes; they are not an independent audit of every language-standard assertion in those notes.
Behavior categories, including signed shift and narrowing statements, follow the source's explicit C23 wording.
Some small concepts naturally admit closely related baseline/transfer boundary judgments; large algorithm/program topics use different subtasks rather than a full arbitrary-code compiler.
Free text accepts listed answers plus the application engine's normalization, not arbitrary equivalent prose or all valid C spellings.
